data.title: Yemen - Malaysia betting prediction for 17 November 2026
data.content: Now for the squad situation, which I think is the key to this game. Malaysia are without the core of their team for this camp. The association has allowed players from Johor Darul Ta’zim, the country’s strongest club, to rest, while also protecting the club’s AFC ranking. Several Selangor players are out injured, and forward Safawi Rasid has left the squad for family reasons. That leaves an experimental young side: nine members of the squad are under 25, and they’re being led by caretaker coach [...] Here’s how it all stacks up. In their only recent friendly, Malaysia managed two shots on target, an xG of 0.56 and no goals. This time they face Yemen rather than China—a side that held firm against Qatar despite facing 20 shots. Yemen’s coaching staff have made it clear that tightening up defensively is a priority. Malaysia, meanwhile, arrive depleted: no Johor Darul Ta’zim stars, several Selangor players missing, no Safawi, a caretaker coach and nine players under 25. Both teams have had [...] Both teams have had just three days’ rest, and this is their second game of the international window, so rotation and a stop-start rhythm are likely.
